spec.title: AI o11y — Problem Employees
spec.description: Per-user anomaly catch for SupportBot. Surfaces token-glutton bursts (10-50x output tokens for 2 min) and runaway-loop bursts (10-50 calls/min for 3 min) emitted by the supportbot-anomalies k6 scenario. Same panels catch real-world anomalies of the same shape.

spec.title: Top output-token user (5m)
spec.description: User with the highest output-token burn in the last 5 minutes. Catches the token-glutton anomaly (one user requests huge documents).

spec.title: Top call-rate user (5m)
spec.description: User firing the most LLM calls in the last 5 minutes (per minute). Catches the runaway-loop anomaly (one user stuck in a retry loop).

spec.title: Output tokens/min by user — top 5 (5m rate)
spec.description: Output-token rate per acme.com user. A user pegging high above the pack is a token-glutton spike.

spec.title: Calls/min by user — top 5 (5m rate)
spec.description: LLM-call rate per acme.com user. A user pegging 10-50x the others is a runaway-loop spike — k6 anomaly scenario runs 180s bursts.

spec.title: acme.com calls/min by provider (5m rate)
spec.description: All acme.com SB user traffic split by provider. Anomaly bursts pin preferred_provider=ollama so spikes shouldn't move the anthropic line.

spec.title: Top problem conversations (30d)
spec.description: Top SupportBot conversations by $ wasted in the last 30d. Each row is ONE conversation. Raw chat cost on these models is cents — values are scaled × 12 so a notable chat reads as ~$10 instead of $0.83. Click the Conversation cell to open the trace in AI o11y.

spec.expr: (sum by (session_id, user_id) (increase(gen_ai_client_cost_usd_total{user_id=~".+@acme.com",session_id!=""}[30d])) or sum by (session_id, user_id) (max_over_time(gen_ai_user_tokens_total{user_id=~".+@acme.com",session_id!="",gen_ai_token_type="output"}[30d])) * 0) * 12

((sum by (session_id, user_id) (increase(gen_ai_client_cost_usd_total{user_id=~".+@acme.com",session_id!=""}[30d])) or sum by (session_id, user_id) (max_over_time(gen_ai_user_tokens_total{user_id=~".+@acme.com",session_id!="",gen_ai_token_type="output"}[30d])) * 0) * 12) * on(session_id, user_id) (1 - max by (session_id, user_id) (conversation_eval_score{user_id=~".+@acme.com"}) / 100)

spec.title: Worst employees by waste (30d)
spec.description: Per-employee aggregate over the last 24h. Sessions = distinct conversation_ids the employee opened. Inner-joined: only employees with both a cost figure and at least one scored conversation appear.

spec.expr: ((sum by (user_id) (increase(gen_ai_client_cost_usd_total{user_id=~".+@acme.com"}[30d])) or sum by (user_id) (max_over_time(gen_ai_user_tokens_total{user_id=~".+@acme.com",gen_ai_token_type="output"}[30d])) * 0) * 12) * on(user_id) (1 - avg by (user_id) (conversation_eval_score{user_id=~".+@acme.com"}) / 100)

options.content:
### How to read these tables

**Wasted $$** = `Cost × (1 − Eval Score / 100)`. It captures **both** axes of "bad AI usage" — spending money *and* not getting value for it.

- Spend **$100** with an eval score of **80%** → `$100 × (1 − 0.80)` = **$20 wasted**.
- Spend **$100** with an eval score of **0%** → `$100 × (1 − 0)` = **$100 wasted** — every dollar burned.
- Score **100%** wastes **$0** no matter how much they spend — perfect use of the AI budget.

All $$ values are 30-day measured × 12. For **employees** that's a literal annual projection (per-user spend is an ongoing rate). For **conversations** it's a scaling factor — single-chat costs on Haiku and Sonnet are cents, so the × 12 makes the demo-relevant magnitudes (the worst chat is ~$10 wasted, not $0.83) visible at a glance. Eval scores come from an Ollama-driven judge (qwen2.5:14b) running outside the LLM gateway. Inner-joined — rows with blank cells filtered.
